title: Asking for structured output when it makes consumption easier

videos.script: In this course, a program reads the answer next, not a person. That is the only reason to ask for JSON. {{title}} The same message, answered in prose, is fine for somebody on the support team. A router needs a field it can find by name, and a value it can compare. {{prose}} Structure has a price, and here it was the other way round. Left without a format, the model wrote over a hundred tokens a reply. Asked for JSON, it wrote thirty. {{cost}} Then comes the contract. The checks in the harness are a schema in miniature: which keys must be there, which ones may be, and what values each one takes. {{checks}} One line in the prompt, asking for nothing around the JSON, fixes nothing here, because this model never wrapped its answers. It moves two other results the wrong way. Whether yours does is a measurement. {{strict}} The one reply that will not parse is broken inside, at an apostrophe. A lenient parser cannot mend it, and a retry at temperature zero gets the same broken reply three times. {{lenient}} A structured-output mode mends that one. For the rest, you decide what the program does: try again, fall back, or hand it to a person. It never guesses. {{close}}
